correctness.rationale: For any factor product of K_{q_i}, every edge changing coordinate i sits in a unique maximal coordinate clique of size q_i. In counting-free FO^k (k≥3), an edge lies in an a-clique via x,y and a−2 witnesses, for 2≤a≤k. Thus E_j colors edges by min(q_i,k)=j with at most k names. Iterating finite E_j-path distance via three free-variable roles and locally reusable bound names defines, for each finite h, the existence of a distance-h pair with k variable symbols; maximum finite E_j distance in a component equals the number c_j of corresponding coordinate factors. Hence equality of all truncated counts is necessary. Sufficiency: a duplicator maintains coordinatewise equality patterns of k pebbles under a paired factor bijection for alphabets below k, or both≥k, because at most k−1 coordinate values remain on each move. Width-1/2 cases and fixed-d weak-composition count follow; the first differing exact factor multiplicity t gives minimum width t+1 except different factor counts (width3) and one-factor versus product (width2). Independent small mixed-product E_j-component distance checks at k=3,4,5 corroborate; the unbounded-quantifier-rank theorem rests on the pebble argument, not finite check.
